title: Cycle Capacity Allocator — Microtranches & Dynamic Scope-Slicing
creator: Sophie Chen
description: Problem: We repeatedly hit mid-cycle friction when multiple cross-functional projects contend for limited engineering capacity, forcing ad-hoc scope cuts that degrade OKR outcomes. Goal: Design and deliver a lightweight Cycle Capacity Allocator (CCA) pattern that splits a cycle into microtranches of capacity, reserves an elastic surge buffer, and provides deterministic scope-slicing rules for rapid decisions. Success metrics: 1) Reduce unplanned mid-cycle scope cuts by 40% vs baseline; 2) Reduce time-to-decision for scope cuts to <4 hours for critical-path items; 3) Keep predicted vs actual cycle utilization variance within ±10%.
acceptance_criteria: CCA playbook published in Confluence with step-by-step runbook
Automation: simple manifest (YAML) that teams declare priorities, stretch targets, and must-have flags
Pilot run executed for two cross-functional initiatives with post-mortem and utilization report
Stakeholder alignment (GTMs, Eng leads, Design lead) documented and approved
deliverables: Template: microtranche YAML spec + example for runtime team
Automation: small script to compute allocation and slack levels (prototype in GH)
Runbook: scope-slicing decision tree and communication templates
Pilot report with utilization vs forecast dashboard links
comments: 2026-02-10 Sophie Chen: Initial scope and objectives drafted after sync with Eng leadership. Proposed microtranche size = 2 weeks; surge buffer 10% of cycle FTEs. Asking PMs to validate feasibility for Q1 pilots.

2026-02-16 Aisha Kumar: Met with runtime and infra leads. Eng concern: frequent context switches for microtranches <2 weeks. Decision: make microtranche configurable per team; recommend 2-3 weeks default. Eng to produce context-switch cost estimate (ENG-4123).

2026-02-18 Product review: Trade-off discussed — larger tranches reduce switching overhead but reduce scheduling agility. We prioritized reducing mid-cycle scope churn for critical OKRs (customer-facing features).

2026-02-22 Design feedback (Maya Patel): Need a single source-of-truth template for feature priority flags ('must', 'should', 'nice') and clear UX for communicating scope cuts to customers. Design to produce communication copy.

2026-02-25 Ops (Omar Lee): Prototype script uploaded to GH (#6780) that ingests declared priorities and outputs recommended allocations + slack. Flagged edge case: overlapping critical-path across teams — added tie-breaker rule based on OKR impact score.

2026-02-28 Sophie Chen: Scope-slicing decision tree baked into runbook. Added escalation path: if allocation delta >20% then trigger cross-functional triage within 6 hours. Shared draft with VPs for sign-off.

2026-03-01 Aisha Kumar: Approved pilot roster: Runtime, Console, and Platform-Integrations. Pilot kickoff scheduled 2026-03-04. Next action: collect microtranche manifests from teams by 2026-03-02. Assigned follow-ups to Eng leads and EMs.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overhead from frequent microtranches may reduce throughput. Mitigation: conservative default tranche length and optional opt-out for low-context-switch teams.
Risk: Perceived unfairness in allocations. Mitigation: transparent allocation algorithm + appeal window and final escalation to Product Council.
Risk: Tooling complexity. Mitigation: keep initial automation minimal (scripts + spreadsheet) before investing in UI.
Risk: Missing cross-team dependencies. Mitigation: require teams to declare dependencies in manifest; include dependency-check step in allocation script.
